data.name: CabinetDossiers.Subtitle
data.value: Create your clients' dossiers, or ask to erase a dossier the firm no longer handles.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Denied
data.value: Only the firm administrator manages its dossiers. Ask them to create or erase one.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Form.Hint
data.value: The dossier gets its own database and its own encryption key. It opens at once to people with access to the whole firm; grant access to others in “Team and access”.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Empty.Text
data.value: Create the firm's first dossier with “New dossier”.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Erase.Question
data.value: Close this dossier? It will be erased in 30 days unless you cancel.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.NotErasable
data.value: This dossier is declared in the server configuration, or kept on this device: it cannot be erased from Lettra.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Toast.ErasureScheduled
data.value: Dossier “{0}” closed. It will be erased on {1} unless you cancel before then.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Toast.ErasureCancelled
data.value: Erasure cancelled: dossier “{0}” reopens as it was.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Toast.Failed
data.value: The operation did not go through. Try again.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Rule.Create
data.value: Each dossier has its own database and its own encryption key, wrapped by the firm's key. A dossier's data never mixes with another's.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Rule.Erase
data.value: Requesting erasure closes the dossier at once, for everyone. For 30 days you can cancel: the dossier reopens as it was. After that its key is destroyed (its data becomes unreadable, backups included), then its database is deleted.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Rule.Keep
data.value: Before requesting erasure, export what the firm must keep (FEC, document archives): accounting records must still be kept for ten years.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Rule.Declared
data.value: A dossier declared in the server configuration (the firm's own server, the demo), or kept on this device, cannot be erased from Lettra: its database belongs to whoever declared it.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Import.Hint
data.value: The dossier arrives whole, under its original identifier, with its anti-fraud chain still verifiable. It opens straight away to the people who have access to the whole firm.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Import.TooLarge
data.value: This file is larger than 512 MB: it is not a package Lettra can import.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Export.Hint
data.value: The file holds the whole dossier, encrypted with this passphrase: at least 12 characters (four words or more are easy to remember and hard to guess). Lettra does not keep it: write it down somewhere safe, away from the file. Without it, the file can no longer be opened.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Export.Mismatch
data.value: The two passphrases do not match.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Toast.Exported
data.value: Dossier “{0}” exported to the file {1}. Keep the passphrase away from the file.

data.name: CabinetDossiers.Rule.Export
data.value: “Export” puts a whole dossier into a single file, encrypted with a passphrase you choose: its database in the open SQLite format, its documents and its anti-fraud chain. “Import a dossier” takes it back on another Lettra server, a workstation or another online installation. This is also the data portability provided for by the GDPR.
